speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a chest skin lesion; how long has it been present, and have you noticed any changes in its size, color, or shape? Have you experienced any pain, itching, or bleeding from the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; given your diabetes and the lesion's growth, have you noticed any ulceration, crusting, or raised borders? Also, does the lesion appear dark or pigmented? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest skin lesion close-up.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin lesion on the chest. I also have Lesion has increased in size, Not painful, Not itchy. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma. The combination of a rapidly growing, non-tender chest lesion in a diabetic patient is highly suspicious for this malignancy until proven otherwise.
